text:
sara: Hey team, AcmePayments reported inconsistent behavior within the same conversation after yesterday's model rollout. They say identical requests in one session returned two different decisions (approve vs decline).

acme_ops: @sara attaching two responses from the same chat session. We sent the same prompt twice, back-to-back, and got different outcomes. This is blocking our fraud flow. Request IDs: r_0a1b2c3d and r_0a1b2c3e.

sara: Thanks. Can you paste the exact prompt and any headers you used?

acme_ops: Prompt (redacted): "Evaluate transaction: amount=420.00, card_country=US, device_score=0.73, account_age_days=30. Return: APPROVE / DECLINE + short reason."
Headers: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>` `X-Client-Tenant: acme-payments` `X-Request-ID: r_0a1b2c3d`

acme_ops: r_0a1b2c3d -> response: "APPROVE: low risk, device score acceptable."
acme_ops: r_0a1b2c3e -> response: "DECLINE: suspicious pattern, escalate to manual review."

alex: Ugh. That looks like routing/fallback mixing variants mid-session. Any recent rollout?

deploy-bot: canary-rollout: model=gpt-medium-q8 -> target=gpt-small-q4; rollout 15% -> 40% traffic between 2026-03-08T21:00Z and 2026-03-08T22:15Z.

jia: I can take this. Two hypotheses: 1) routing policy switched variants between requests (latency/cost routing) causing different model behaviors, 2) customer session pinning failed so subsequent requests hit different model variants.

matt: I pulled routing logs for tenant=acme-payments around ts r_0a1b2c3d/e. I see r_0a1b2c3d -> gpt-medium-q8 (model_variant_id mv-420m); r_0a1b2c3e -> gpt-small-q4 (mv-109s). Both served from the same node pool but different quant/arch.

jia: That matches. gpt-small-q4 has a different prompt scoring distribution and we did see behavior change on fraud prompts in perf tests. If session pinning is enabled they should stay on mv-420m; if not, routing can switch. Did customer set a stable model pin?

acme_ops: We don't pin in our integration. We rely on consistent behavior.

sara: For mitigation, can we 1) pin their tenant to mv-420m, or 2) roll back the canary? Customer wants immediate fix.

jia: Quick fixes: I can add a tenant-level override to pin traffic to mv-420m for AcmePayments (will take ~10m). Longer: investigate why session affinity didn't keep them on the same variant — possible cache key mismatch for `X-Client-Tenant` header.

matt: I'll check affinity logs and the cache key hash. Early sign: some requests lost `X-Client-Tenant` in the internal proxy when under burst, causing fallback to routing default.

alex: Can you share the curl we asked for? I'm trying to repro locally.

acme_ops: Example curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'X-Client-Tenant: acme-payments' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium-q8","input":"Evaluate transaction...","request_id":"r_0a1b2c3d"}'
```

jia: Repro tip: call twice without changing headers, but also try removing the X-Client-Tenant header to see behavior change.

matt: Action items: (1) Jia will pin tenant -> mv-420m now. (2) I will trace proxy logs for header stripping and produce a short RCA. (3) Alex/sara will inform AcmePayments and offer rollback or pin.

sara: I'll notify the customer and ask if they want pin or rollback.

acme_ops: Please pin for now, that solves it fast. We'll discuss long-term. Appreciate the quick response. :pray:

jia: Pining started -> tenant override applied for acme-payments -> traffic confirmed to mv-420m for new requests (trace sample IDs: t_77aa, t_77ab).

matt: Found a proxy bug where `X-Client-Tenant` was dropped on retry path for ~0.6% of requests under heavy load. Raising P0 ticket with eng-infra.

alex: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the customer notes and keep this thread updated.

sara: Closing loop: customer pinned, behavior stable on their tests. We'll keep RCA in a separate ticket. :white_check_mark:
